name: Breadcrumb
summary: Shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy, with a link to each level above it.
description: A breadcrumb lists the pages above the current one, from the top of the hierarchy down, each as a link, and ends with the current page, which is not a link. It tells people where they are and lets them go up one or several levels in one activation. It is a navigation landmark of its own, separate from the main navigation.

anatomy.description: Root: a navigation landmark named Breadcrumb. Carries the size and the states forced for review.
One level: its link (or the current page) and, except for the last, a separator. Takes the states of its link.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Name of the page, as its title.

properties.name: Destination
properties.description: Where the level links to. Ignored for the last item, which is the current page.

anatomy.description: The link to a level above, or the current page as plain text marked current.
Chevron glyph of the icon font between two levels. Hidden from assistive technology; the list conveys the order.

properties.name: Landmark label
properties.description: Name of the navigation landmark, so it is told apart from the other navigation regions of the page.

properties.name: Items
properties.description: The levels from the top of the hierarchy to the current page, last.

states.description: A link to a level above: underlined, in the secondary text color.
Pointer over a link: the primary text color. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on a link. Shows the shared focus ring around it; pointer focus shows none.
The last item, the current page: plain text in the primary color, not underlined, exposed as the current page.

notes: Levels flow on one line and wrap when the space runs out; a separator follows every level but the last.
Each link is at least 24 px high; the gap between a link, its separator and the next link comes from container.gap.

name.text: The landmark is named by its label property (aria-label on the web), Breadcrumb by default, which tells it apart from the other navigation regions. Each link is named by its text; the current page is marked as such.

keyboard.action: Moves focus through the links in order; the current page is not focusable.

guidelines.text: A breadcrumb trail is a list of links to the parent pages of the current page in hierarchical order, contained in a navigation landmark with a label, and the current page is marked current.
Use a nav element with aria-label="Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list; each level is a list item with a link, and the last one carries aria-current="page".
Give each navigation landmark of a page a unique label, so people moving between landmarks can tell the breadcrumb from the main navigation.
A breadcrumb tells people where they are within the set of pages, beyond what the page title says.
Each link is named by the page it leads to, so its purpose is clear from its text; keep the breadcrumb in the same place and order on every page.
The current page is plain text, not a link to itself; it is distinguished by weight and color and by its position, never by color alone.
Link text contrasts 12.87:1 (light) and 8.80:1 (dark) with the default surface, the current page 19.07:1 and 11.27:1; the separators are decoration (6.08:1 and 6.36:1 anyway).
The separators are decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read between the links.
A visible focus indicator appears around the focused link; links are underlined so they are identified without color.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.
Links are at least 24 CSS pixels high; in a wrapped trail the inline spacing keeps them apart.
Color transitions of the links are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

references.title: APG: Breadcrumb pattern, roles, states and properties

APG: Naming with aria-label (a navigation region)

WCAG technique ARIA11: ARIA landmarks to identify regions of a page

guidelines: Each level is the title of its page, as short as the page allows: Settings, Members, Ada Lovelace.
The first level is the root of the hierarchy (Home, Projects), the last the current page.
Never truncate the current page; shorten intermediate levels if the trail is too long.

decisions.text: A breadcrumb is a navigation landmark named Breadcrumb holding an ordered list; the last item is the current page, marked current and not linked; a chevron separates the levels.
Links are underlined in the secondary text color and turn primary on hover; the current page is primary text without underline; separators take the tertiary icon color.
Two sizes: small (12 px text, 16 px separator) and medium (14 px, 20 px, the default); links are at least 24 px high, 4 px apart from their separators.
